episode_title: Rebuilding America's Water: A D-Minus Grade and a $1 Trillion Bill

real_qa.q: What is the current rating of water infrastructure in the United States according to the American Society of Civil Engineers?
real_qa.r: The American Society of Civil Engineers gave a rating of D-minus for the water infrastructure currently in the United States. Additionally, approximately one trillion dollars needs to be spent over the next 20 years just to maintain existing infrastructure.
real_qa.requete: American Society Civil Engineers water infrastructure rating USA

real_qa.q: What is the Faraday reactor and how does it disinfect water differently than conventional electrocoagulation methods?
real_qa.r: The Faraday reactor uses alternating current at less than 12 volts of power, compared to conventional direct current electrocoagulation which uses 50 to 120 volts. It works by using electroporation to cut through cell walls of viruses and bacteria at a molecular level, combined with an advanced reduction process to break chemical chains like PFAS, followed by a dissolved air flotation device to separate solids without requiring membranes, filters, or chemical solutions.
real_qa.requete: Faraday reactor water disinfection technology how it works

real_qa.q: How many cyber-attacks by Iran targeted water treatment facilities and what vulnerability did they exploit?
real_qa.r: Multiple cities and facilities were cyber-attacked by Iran a few weeks before this episode was recorded. The attacks exploited vulnerabilities in old PLC systems and SCADA systems. In one instance, an operator discovered the breach only when he saw his mouse moving on its own, as the attacker had gained remote access through these systems.
real_qa.requete: Iran cyber attack water treatment facilities PLC SCADA vulnerability

real_qa.q: What are the main vertical markets for Water.com's water treatment technology?
real_qa.r: Water.com operates in four main verticals: real estate and aquatics including Disney and Kalahari resorts; wastewater, sewage, and drinking water treatment representing a $600 billion TAM worldwide; on-site reuse for industrial manufacturers like Nestle, wineries, breweries, and data centers; and closed-loop systems for manufacturing facilities seeking to treat and reuse their contaminated water.
real_qa.requete: Water.com vertical markets applications industries served

real_qa.q: According to the World Health Organization, what is the current global water crisis status?
real_qa.r: The World Health Organization came out earlier in the year stating that the world has officially gone into water bankruptcy, meaning the balance of plus and minus assets versus liabilities no longer maps. The world is taking out more water than is being replenished.
real_qa.requete: World Health Organization water bankruptcy global crisis

guest.bio_context: Kevin Gass is the CEO and Chairman of Water.com, a company birthed from a larger conglomerate that has completed 14,000 to 15,000 water treatment projects over the last 60 years. The organization has worked extensively with membranes, filters, chemicals, biologicals, drinking water facilities, and sewage treatment facilities of all shapes and sizes before developing its proprietary Faraday reactor technology.
